We present HyperDegrade, an innovative end-to-end CPU rate throttling
management strategy, divided into three main components: ThrottleMap, a
database of CPU throttling policies, organized by performance and temperature
ranges and linked through a directed graph; a selective update mechanism that
optimizes CPU throughput by evaluating new processor specifications against
existing ThrottleMap entries; and HyperDegrade, a dynamic throttling algorithm
used on the CPU, which monitors CPU temperatures, applies corresponding
throttleMap entries, and employs efficient and accurate linear regression to
determine optimal throughput frequencies based on CPU performance goals and
temperature-dependent constraints. Experimental evaluations with diverse
synthetic and real-world workloads on various CPU systems demonstrate the
superiority of HyperDegrade over existing rate throttling strategies, exhibiting
lower temperatures, reduced energy consumption, better performance, and
throughput, surpassing baselines by margins of up to 8.7^{\circ}C, 12.4%,
2.1%, and 42.6%, respectively, while also displaying upgrades of up to 8GHz
and 100MHz in CPU system throughput frequency resolution.

Our study introduces a novel knot theory move, the rescaling move, combining it with the traditional Alexander move and the delta-move to develop a new unknotting algorithm for traditional and welded knots. Notably, our algorithm distinguishes itself as the first polynomial-time procedure for proving the unknotting status in these categories. Using the new rescaling move, we demonstrate how certain knots, including the trefoil and the figure-eight, can be readily classified as true knots under both traditional and welded distinctions, and thus are also instantly recognizable as true knots in the traditional framework.

We demonstrate that the Fox-Hatcher loop constitutes a Vassiliev characteristic within the third order, furthermore establishing that among all Vassiliev characteristics of order three up to a specific equivalence, it is unique in its particular nature. We also explore other distinctive features of this characteristic and provide an algorithm to produce its geodesic representation in a way that is computationally efficient.

In the field of multi-agent systems, tactical collaboration aims to enable groups of individual agents to work together to solve problems beyond their individual capabilities by sharing information and strategies. While research into optimal collaborative tactics often assumes access to complete and instantaneous knowledge of the environment, real-world applications typically operate under limitations in communication and computation that must be factored into optimal tactics. This paper presents a Markov Decision Process (MDP) model for tactical multi-agent collaboration that incorporates the energy costs of sharing information and strategies, and introduces a more efficient variant of the popular centralized decentralized policy gradient (CD3G) algorithm to accelerate the training of a common value function. Through rigorous testing using a multi-agent version of the star topology maze navigation environment, the improved algorithm outperformed the original in terms of task completion efficiency.

The concept of federated learning has been promoted as a method to conduct secure machine learning on a large-scale basis. In a setup known as vertical federated learning, models are trained to machine learning tasks while preserving user data privacy and facilitating efficient learning across machines learning databases of size and variety. Nevertheless, the security of algorithms in vertical federated learning frameworks against pragmatic assaults that aim to machine learning models to undesirable, harmful predictions with specific inputs remain unexplored issues. This study delves into the issues of privacy and information sensitivity in vertical federated learning settings, presents several assaults that can result in the leakage of sensitive information and the desired leakage of sensitive information and the desired machine learning models' behavior. In addition, we examine the issues of information sensitivity versatility and assault efficiency in various settings of vertical federated learning, and investigate the mathematical properties and efficacy of the proposed methods on multiple real-world datasets and settings. Furthermore, we also develop counter-methods to mitigate the risks of information sensitivity leakage and demonstrate the desired machine learning models' desired predictions with specific inputs remain undesirable, harmful with the intended purpose of the desired assaults.

Traditional kernel methods, such as those based on diffusion graphs or neural networks, often require a significant amount of computational effort and memory, particularly when dealing with large-scale data. In response to these limitations, we introduce the kernel estimator of random features (rfrf), which offers a memory-efficient and rapid alternative. The rfrf kernel estimator leverages the statistical characteristics of the data to determine the parameters of the feature map, thereby ensuring that the resulting features preserve the geometric relationships of the original data in the high-dimensional space. We support this claim with theoretical backing and further validate the rfrf kernel estimator through comparisons with established methods in the realm of support vector classification. The experiment demonstrates that the rfrf kernel estimator maintains the Euclidean distances of data points in their transformed space, facilitating the effective application of classical kernel methods.

It has long been known that any finite simple group can be embedded as a subgroup within the symmetric group $S_n$, but achieving a high word length for these embeddings has proven consistently challenging. In this study, we aim to increase the word length of these embeddings to at least $\frac{144}{7} \times 5 \log_2 n$. Additionally, we claim a similar result for embedding any finite simple subgroup of $S_n$, denoted as $G$, with an equivalent condition in terms of natural parameters.

This research focuses on conformal transformations of a hypersurface $\Sigma$ within the sphere $S^{n+2}$ and aims to establish the non-existence of specific submanifolds with particular properties. Specifically, we prove that any hypersurface $\Sigma$ in the sphere $S^{n+2}$ that is conformally equivalent to a compact oriented hypersurface with non-negative curvature in its own right cannot have a negative Mobius curvature. As a direct consequence, this implies that the Fubini-Study complex projective spaces $\mathbb{C}P^m$ with its standard metric cannot be smoothly deformed into a compact manifold with non-negative scalar curvature through conformal transformations.

In modern multi-antenna wireless systems that use simultaneous information and power transmission, optimizing resource allocation is essential to balance the amount of information transmitted and electricity harvested. A key issue in this process is how to allocate resources when interference changes based on the amount of electricity harvested, making the problem highly complex. By limiting received interference in specific time-frequency slots, researchers have started breaking this joint optimization into manageable subproblems. However, existing studies focus on single-user systems and ignore critical factors such as power splitting and flow control. Focusing on an uplink OFDMA system with energy harvesting, this paper investigates optimal resource allocation to maximize system utility while ensuring minimum electricity harvested for information decoding. Using convex optimization techniques and duality theory, researchers derived the optimal distribution of resources, revealing interesting insights into the interplay between information transmission and electricity harvesting in SWIPT systems.

Cayley graphs, having undergone significant applications in computer science and combinatorics, find an intriguing analogy with the structure of the interweb in recent research. By representing the interweb as directed and undirected random graphs with directed cycles, researchers were able to identify the structural features of Cayley graphs within the interweb's complex network. Specifically, the probability distribution of the number of non-redundant links per website was found to match the probability distribution of the number of generators in groups with certain characteristics. Notably, the median number of non-redundant links per website in the interweb corresponds to Grouppedia's 'twin prime' graph, where most websites with only a few non-redundant links have incomplete connections and only a small number of websites with a larger number of non-redundant links have complete connections.

The detection sensitivity of seismic-affected low-frequency bands in interferometric gravitational wave detectors can be enhanced by extending the length of their suspended mirrors. However, this method is limited due to the need to minimize mirrors' vibration amplitudes. The sloshing Sagnac interferometer, a novel design derived from the sagnac configuration, offers improved high-frequency responses through the intentional oscillation of its oppositely suspended mirrors. Theoretical and numerical analyses reveal that the sloshing Sagnac interferometer's field flatness and gain are comparable to traditional Michelson interferometers,而其响应特性则可借助驱动线圈轻松优化以提供显著优势。The downsides of the sloshing Sagnac design, including the necessity of precise alignment and increased complexity, may be countered by its simplified optics arrangement and lack of requiring beam splitter replacement. The potential for the sloshing Sagnac design to serve as an effective intermediary between gravitational wave sensors and advanced detectors by incorporating its design features is also explored.

This paper discusses the unique visibility relationship in extreme large-amplitude small-cell systems and accesses dynamics in a multi-cellular network. As link estimation methods become more efficient and signal interference drops with the number of users, assessing cell transmission visibilities and their intersections is crucial for advanced access protocols. Using a Markov random field model, we analyze the visibility relationships between cells and assess various protocols, such as those based on geometric distance, random selection, and intersections weighting in an extreme large-amplitude small-cell systems. In an extensive simulation study, we observe that geometric distance and random selection methods perform similarly, but neither is optimal in deciding cell visibility relationships. Furthermore, we note that even a basic intersection-based weighting method outperforms the other two methods in determining cell visibilities.

Recent high-resolution submillimeter and millimeter continuum observations have revealed that planetary disks contain a variety of small-scale structures. However, theoretical models aiming to replicate this complexity often struggle due to an abundance of poorly understood physical mechanisms. Recent discoveries of key parameters governing the growth of magnetic fields within these disks may enable general purpose magnetic instability models to better reproduce what is observed. Comparing model predictions with observed data from complex planetary disks will provide valuable feedback to refine magnetic instability models and potentially guide the search for small-scale structures in other well-studied planetary disks. Our investigation specifically explored a model of magnetic instability that incorporates multiple sources of disk complexity, including careful treatment of magnetic fields, gas and dust dynamics, and effects of gravitational forces. Then, we examined the structure of simulated disks at a resolution comparable to that of current and future observations, finding that most small-scale features would likely be detectable by current observations and some might even be detectable by next-generation instruments.

A novel axial tensor current interaction has been recently proposed and, when incorporated into our tailored code, demonstrates significant significance. Notably, it contributes roughly 20% to the total strength of the electric dipole operator in both mean field and random phase approximations. In both $^{16}$O and $^{40}$Ca, this tensor contribution accounts for approximately 20 MeV of total strength, concentrating near the threshold of electric dipole resonance. Consequently, the tensor contribution's impact on the equation of state, skyrme energy density functional, and neutron skin thickness is found to be negligible. In contrast, within neutron stars, it contributes roughly 10-15 MeV per nucleon to the total energy density at saturation saturation density density. Further examination of the tensor contribution through external proton decay energy also reveals a range of 8-12 MeV. Further research is required to delve deeper into the tensor contribution's effect on the saturation properties of nuclear matter.

This research examines the robustness of Molmer-Sorensen gates in terms of their resistance to frequency errors in a variety of scenarios. It demonstrates that the performance of these gates remains stable across different conditions, particularly when the temperatures of trapped ions differ or during experiments involving warm ions following their natural liberation from traps. It further reveals that the temperature disparity between the ions does not necessarily result in an increased error rate; rather, it finds that the optimal condition for minimizing errors is when the balance of motion between the ions matches their difference in frequency. It also finds that a non-intuitive 37-degree phase offset offers the highest robustness against frequency errors. Lastly, it proposes that the molmer-sorensen gates can be considered highly resilient, allowing them to be executed successfully even with a significant frequency discrepancy of nearly 1 kHz, as observed in an aluminum-80 pair with varying trapped conditions.

Using Dirac cones in boron, we conduct a first-hand study of the pure crystal structure through advanced embedded atom method calculations combined with linear augmented plane wave method, which reveals the origin of boron's unique properties as a 2D Dirac metal with multiple bands and robust conductive behavior, resisting disruption from external factors.

We have created a comprehensive model of the NA62 experiment's potential in searching for a neutral lepton from extended Standard Model theories via the $K^+ \to \pi^0 e^+ N$ decay, which requires the decay to be highly suppressed. By analyzing an estimated $10^{15}$ charged kaon failures, we anticipate being able to confirm rare decay processes with a length of $10^{-12}$ seconds. This will enable us to discover neutral leptons with a mass of up to 500 MeV, given their rare decay rate of $10^{-9}$ and mixing with an established particle of at least $0.3 \times 10^{-6}$, or longer-lived kaon clusters that result from rare interactions and have a duration of more than a few tens of picoseconds.

Our investigation aims to enhance the neural language model's text generation capabilities through a novel approach called the $N$-gram Neural Residual Learning framework. This framework focuses on addressing the basic grammar and structural aspects of a language through $n$-gram models, while leveraging neural networks to master the more intricate semantic nuances. Our proposed framework consists of two main components: a base $n$-gram model that handles the fundamental aspects of the language, and a neural network-based modifier that adds layers of meaning. Through a series of experiments, we discovered the following key key points by applying this framework across various $N$ values from 3 to 11: utilizing a neural network as a modifier can significantly boost the accuracy of task-oriented tasks such as machine translation, paratranslation, and speech recognition by 0.64%, 1.04%, and 1.44% respectively. Our analysis further reveals that the most beneficial information for the neural network is contained within the 5-$gram$ model, and using a transformer-based architecture along with increased training data can further optimize the results. Furthermore, our framework has also been successfully extended to a more challenging semantic understanding dataset, achieving a 1.25% improvement in performance. Reconstructing 3D faces from unstructured 2D images poses complex challenges due to diverse facial expressions, obscured features, and vast inter-personal differences. These difficulties are significantly magnified in tasks involving large-scale predictions. This study presents SADRNet, a novel end-to-end framework producing highly accurate face predictions at any scale, utilizing innovative self-aligned regression modules and an innovative hybrid loss function. The proposed method employs two separated network branches, an identity-aware branch utilizing idntity embedding to predict idiosyncratic id features and a universal face feature, and an expression-aware branch employing bounding box normalization to express-specific features and universal face feature. The shared features from both network branches are jointly optimized in order to produce id- and expression-aware universal face features through a dual face attention mechanism. In an effort to jointly optimize the predicted heatmaps and triangulated 3D landmarks, an innovative hybrid loss function is employed, integrating a 3D landmark reconstruction loss function to encourage mutual consistency between the heatmaps and 3D landmarks. The proposed method is extensively evaluated on four publicly available datasets including the widely recognized AFH, I3D, IMPE, and the newly released ERH datasets, demonstrating superior performance in comparison to the state-of-the-art methodologies in terms of face reconstruction and 3D landmark prediction performance.

In our study, we analyzed linear and nonlinear inflationary perturbation theory during the $ matter  $ era to determine the possibility of forming primordial black holes (PBHs) as a consequence of inflationary fluctuations. We discovered that a specific condition, expressed as R/r > 1, dictates the transition from the matter era to the radiation era for PBHs. Here, R represents the dimensionless curvature fluctuation and r denotes the ratio of a field's time derivative to Hubble's parameter times itself. We then investigated how the spectrum of the field contributes to the probability distribution and the resulting PBH mass fraction. We found that even the highest amplification of PBH formation may fall short of explaining the dark matter abundance. However, by comparing our theoretical predictions with previous studies, we established a viable scenario for PBH formation that could account for the observed gamma-ray background.

For any ordered tree with n+1 distinct labels assigned to its nodes based on increasing values from 1 to n+1, the concept of "deepest vertices" refers to the nodes with the highest position in the overall tree structure regardless of their vertical spacing. Researchers are calling these nodes "colossal vertices". When all nodes of a particular ordered tree that have the smallest or largest possible values among colossal vertices are removed, three new types of sorted trees emerge as a result - minimal, maximal, and superminimal-sorted trees. Additionally, the corresponding sets of possible labeled ordered trees for each of these sorted tree categories have been examined, and the characteristics of their generating functions have been examined, revealing that the minimal and superminimal-sorted trees comply with an algebraic equation, whereas maximal-sorted trees conform to a non-commutative polynomial ring.

This investigation involves an exploration of the capability of image-based recognition systems to streamline the effort required for the aggregation of election data. Currently, various entities produce raw data in dataless document formats, necessitating the use of manual data entry methods, which are prone to human error and strain the resources of the organizations responsible for tabulating results. The proposed solution, iOCR, incorporates the use of optical recognition technology to process these documents, converting them into digital data automatically. The findings obtained through this method demonstrate an 18% increase in speed compared to the manual entry process, while also reducing the presence of human error and making the effort required for data entry easier to manage. The code used for this investigation is available online at https://github.com/GeertVanWolferen/iOCR-Election-Datasets/.

In a time series model using an autoregressive approach, an economic or financial variable can be represented as a result of past influences, with the relevant historical information encapsulated in an information matrix. The selection of lagged variables for an optimal model typically relies on information criteria or other methods to an extent, with the number of lagged variables often chosen with some flexibility, as long as the essential information is captured. In this research, an innovative and unconventional scenario is explored where the information matrix of the relevant historical information is nearly zero due to an extremely high frequency, effectively equating an information subset to its full counterpart but with significantly reduced fidelity. In an framework that is linear and probabilistic, it is possible to show that the higher frequency model can be an effective alternative, with adjusted R-squared values approaching unity and the variability of an error term approaching the original level. Through an examination of an artificial dataset and an application to US macroeconomic data, the study reveals the intriguing potential of an higher frequency model to closely resemble its lower frequency counterpart, offering a new perspective on the relationship between time series models at different frequencies.

This paper explores the challenges of deciding on storage procurement in a distributed setting where the future energy prices and an agent's risk tolerance are unpredictable. By formulating the issue as an Markov decision process, we initially capture it in a risk-aware framework and then, under certain conditions, generalize to a cautious decision-making approach. To achieve this, we integrate the risk considerations into a cautious self-planning strategy, resulting in an approximate policy that ensures safety while minimizing long-term costs. To further reduce information requirements and enhance scalability, we develop two scalable algorithmic variations. Through numerical tests based on a real-day-ahead electricity price dataset, our methods are validated, demonstrating reliable performance and scalability.

A fundamental approach to understanding atmospheric circulation on exoplanets and planets employs simplified two-dimensional circulation models. To further refine this understanding, incorporating three-dimensional effects via radiation is crucial. Using a range of models with varying scales of turbulence and temperature fluctuations, we examined how atmospheric circulation evolves under different conditions on hot Jupiters, Venus-like planets, and super-Earths. Findings reveal that extreme conditions lead to rapid temperature variations that impede the development of typical atmospheric patterns, resulting in excessively variation-prone systems. Conversely, hot Jupites with very fast rotation speeds develop exaggerated wind velocities beyond the range where they have a significant impact on atmospheric temperatures. At both ends of the spectrum, the unique interaction between inertia forces and either radiative processes or variation-prone systems dominate and shape the circulation models, limiting their applicability to hot Jupiters, Venus-like planets, and high-density super-Earths. Mid-range models reveal that several planets may exhibit extreme thermal inertia with massive seasonal variations that could shape their unique day-night patterns.

Over-time, our machine teaching algorithm has successfully fine-tuned deep neural networks on ImageNet with 28GB of RAM, eliminating the need for pre-trained models. Our method rewires a high-capacity deep neural network, drawing on meticulous analysis and experimental testing to solve the problem of training these networks dynamically on ImageNet. By eliminating the necessity for sparse gradient descent, we removed multiple memory bottlenecks, enabling direct optimization of network parameters in a single, large batch. Our investigations revealed critical insights into the interplay between batch size, learning rate, and generalization, and our resulting robust learning technique outperformed comparable methods, consistently securing top-5 accuracy in the 2021 ImageNet Challenge with 0.765.

Silicon-based quantum computing relies on the precise management of donor nuclear and electronic spins within its multi-valley conduction band. Although previous studies have effectively modeled ci in a single conduction band valley, the interconnected ci across all relevant weight valleys has received less attention. Using the CIT code and integrating the multi-valley theory, we simulated ci-linked donor configurations, both isolated and under an external magnetic field, across all relevant weight valleys. Precise calculations of ci matrix elements were made possible by incorporating corrections to the overlap and exchange integrals. Notable results indicate that the ci matrix elements are of the same magnitude for all relevant weight valleys, albeit with slight variations. Furthermore, we observed unique behavior in the temperature dependence of the exchange and splitting matrix elements. These findings are invaluable for the development of multi-valley CIT-based quantum computing.

Recent advances in solid-state physics have spurred interest in quantum point contacts made from two-dimensional (2D) hole gases within HgTe quantum wells. Unlike typical HgTe quantum wells, quantum trench structures exhibit unique characteristics: holes confined between thin conducting barriers exhibit extremely high mobility and very narrow energy gap transitions. This research explores the transport properties of HgTe quantum trench contacts at high frequencies and reveals the energy and momentum asymmetry of hole bands affecting scattering rates. Notably, higher hole bands demonstrate backscatterability over long distances due to large helical momentum. A neutron-scattering experiment revealed an exceptionally small spin-orbit-coupling-induced hole gap of 18 micro-eV in 45 nm wide quantum trench samples.

In this paper, a novel Mixed Time-Division Multiple Access (TDMA) protocol is introduced for 5G networks, combining cell-specific uplink and downlink signals. To optimize signal allocation and minimize interference, machine learning and game theory are harnessed, resulting in a comprehensive model that integrates Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) with non-cooperative games. Numerical results validate the efficacy of this approach.

In this work, we highlight the significance of being able to efficiently obtain gradient information from Hamiltonian Neural Networks (HNNs), as long as certain conditions are met. These conditions are fulfilled by widely used neural network architectures. We provide an analytical explanation of how HNN gradient computation is achieved at a cost nearly identical to the forward computation, making them feasible for iterative and recurrent training methods that involve gradient-based updates for constrained systems. Our proposed constrained optimization algorithm, based on simulated Hamiltonian dynamics, demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach. Experimental results also confirm the efficiency of obtaining gradient information from HNNs and the success of our constrained optimization algorithm in improving the overall performance.

The rapid expansion of automatic methods for creating machine learning algorithms, including large-scale models such as LLMs, has facilitated significant advancements in complex tasks that were once beyond our reach. Despite their benefits, these automatic methods have also given rise to concerns regarding inaccuracies and biases, posing potential risks in applications where mistakes could have serious consequences. To address this issue, researchers have generally turned to high-performing automatic frameworks, yet this approach is unsuitable for sensitive applications where trust in the system's outputs is crucial and requires explainability and accountability. In this study, we introduce a novel online multi-agent system designed to incorporate human feedback in the form of ratings of confidence and explanations, in both acceptable and unacceptable situations. Notably, our method ensures the integrity of the training data by preventing duplicate entries, thus enhancing its diversity. Our proposed framework has been evaluated on human-simple classification tasks using two distinct datasets, and our results indicate significant improvements in accuracy and robustness when reinforced with a sequential online learning approach.

We construct quantum invariants for 2-chains within a rectangular prism under various complexities, drawing inspiration from and diverging from the invariants established by Friedl, Kim, and Kwon. These new invariants satisfy a volumetric inequality, confirming a prior conjecture they had posed, and they are distinguished by two key characteristics that they differentiate between, thus expanding the quantum Torus Bezier invariant family and potentially offering a stronger distinction than the standard Homology type.

Exploring the potential of word sense disambiguation (WSD) in medical text understanding, this study investigates the impact of contextual information on performing this task. Specifically, the effectiveness of various context sizes and the use of Gloss context for a medical word sense disambiguation task is analyzed. By comparing the performance of different context types, this research focuses on the ability of structural and semantic features to accomplish the task. The results show that more extensive context sizes lead to improved performance and the Gloss context alone can successfully accomplish the task when utilizing feature sets derived from the Word2Vec model. Additionally, the inclusion of additional textual information from co-occurrences beyond the gloss box significantly boosts the performance.

A novel representation of the reciprocal Gamma function is introduced, filling the gap in a previously proposed integral expression that was only partially defined. This new formulation is not isolated, but rather part of a broader class of similar calculations parameterized by arbitrary test functions. A set of comparable calculations yields analogous results to those previously discovered by other researchers, including an alternative derivation of a specific formula. Furthermore, this class of calculations enables the straightforward evaluation of the reciprocal Gamma function at a set of particular values.

Use a topological approach to identify the presence of top quarks in hadron-nucleus interactions, such as those involving protons. A distinctive feature of top quark decay is its characteristic single high-energy particle followed by additional particles with lower energy, which stands out clearly even without knowledge of the nucleus fragmentation process. This approach is applied to data from anti-neutritino (ice) neutrino interactions collected by the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and reveals the first evidence of top quark generation in these interactions, with a significance of 4.2 sigma. Furthermore, proposed limits on top quark production are more restrictive than those previously set by other experiments, specifically in relation to incoherent deep inelastic scattering cross-sections.

This year's second iteration of the Benchmark for Intent Understanding Beyond SQL across Domains requires participants to build parsers in two areas: simple text-to-schema linking and text-to-SQL parsing, with a cross-domain setup where the training, validation, and testing datasets differ in schema. Text-to-schema parsing takes input data and generates a structured JSON output that maps to the target schema, while SQL parsing converts the text along with the schema into an SQL query matching the intended dataset. Exception handling is also a requirement for both parsers.

A proposed solution in this benchmark involves training separate models for simple text-to-schema parsing and text-toSQL parsing, in their respective domains. It combines the models' outputs to create the final result.

To handle multiple domains, the benchmark sees a test where the training, validation, and testing datasets differ in schema, requiring a new solution proposal using a supportive task. It uses a single model to handle text-to-schema parsing across multiple domains and integrates the proposed supportive task with a Cross-Attention based ensemble method.

Results show the proposed solution achieving the top ranking with a mean score of 0.740, while the supportive task alone also delivers promising outcomes. It demonstrates the effectiveness of integrating multiple models to handle data discrepancies.

Experimental findings further validate the effectiveness of integrating multiple models despite data discrepancies.

This discussion delves into the complexities of implementing differential privacy (DP) to protect social network data for a variety of data analysis purposes. The unique characteristics of graph-organized data complicate DP implementation due to the varying levels of anonymity and the interdependent nature of data within the graph structure. The complexities continue to grow when considering different organizational graphs and the different analysis purposes the data is intended for. We explore these challenges and potential solutions, considering both theoretical and practical considerations, and present several case studies that illustrate the challenges of applying DP to graph-organized data, considering different analysis purposes and organizational structures. This discussion is relevant to a wide range of data on interconnected devices, including online reviews, transaction records, search logs, and modern privacy-preserving technologies such as ContactTracer and Apple's ATT framework. We examine various definitions of DP in relation to graph-organized data, considering sensing purposes, sharing purposes, and general computation purposes.

The vast amount of imaging and spectroscopic data anticipated from the Euclid survey, which is set to begin in October 2026, will enable numerous fascinating "guest scientist" investigations into various phenomena such as galactic evolution and structure formation. Despite being primarily designed to focus on dark energy and dark matter, for which its primary camera and spectrometer are particularly suited, the Euclid telescope's capabilities will also facilitate an in-depth study of galaxies both present-day and in the distant past. However, to fully capitalize on its capabilities and engage with these exciting areas of research, it is crucial to effectively involve the upcoming cosmology community in preparing for Euclid's legacy research using its impressive capabilities to investigate the history and formation of galaxies.

A new stochastic approach has been developed to derive the quantum hydrodynamics equations, building upon initial works by Pusey and Balescu. This random quasi-phase space method, which incorporates uniquely determined interacting Lennard-Jones potentials, enables the derivation of a set of coupled hydrodynamics equations, including Euler's equation for momentum, the mass continuity equation, a new 'variance continuity equation', and an modified energy equation, all subject to source terms and advection terms. All variables evolve dynamically and depend on time, while in the non-relativistic limit, these equations converge to their familiar forms. Furthermore, in a specific limit where the interparticle distance approaches the de Broglie wavelength, the r-matrix theory emerges in its natural form. This approach provides a consistent framework for both theoretical and numerical investigations, linking various hydrodynamics descriptions of interacting bosons in a coherent manner.

Consider two related sequences of letters, and let's say we're given specific letters a and A, and other letters in between. Now, instead of randomly choosing letters between a and A, we'll pick them from the sequences given. If we repeat this process n times and calculate the average of the selected letters, the average will typically fall within a certain range as n grows larger. It's been found that the rate at which this average falls outside a certain range is usually the same as $e^{-c_n}$, and for many cases, the rate is actually constant, meaning $c_n = cn$. However, there are also instances where the rate varies over time, meaning $c_n$ changes with $n$, which is not seen often. This is in contrast to another scenario, involving independently chosen letters, where $n$ is the only factor determining the rate, and not a situation found nature seems to prefer.

This study focuses on a "region minimizing surface" within a sphere $S^{n-1}$, which effectively separates the space into two distinct parts, each containing a specific set of points $A$ and $B$. We demonstrate that in dimensions up to 12, there always exists such a surface optimizing a particular metric related to the area it covers. In higher dimensions specifically 13 and 14, an analogous result holds true for more complex sets $A$ and $B$ than simple points. We also explore the characteristics of these surface minimizing surfaces and their implications.

A region beyond the extended normal deformation shell model in nickel isotopes is reported.
The extended normal deformation shell model is found to be valid in $^{64}$Ni, indicating that extended 2+1d5/2-2p3/2 and 2+1d5/2-2p1/2 tensor forces, acting oppositely, result in comparable T=0 and T=1 quadrupole forces that allow for the stable existence of both high-spin tensor and low-spin tensor-bohr deformation energy surfaces at any angular momentum.
This finding is unprecedented and has never been observed before.
A strong, inverse relationship between the T=0 and T=1 2+ energy states is discovered in even-isospin nickel isotopes with a 2+1d5/2-2p3/2 tensor-bohr deformation driving force that applies to all of them.
This indicates that the 2+1d5/2-2p3/2 tensor force, acting in opposition to the mean-field deformation force, leads to a crossover from pseudo-spontaneous to spontaneous symmetry breaking in the 2p3/2 or 2p1/2 shell, respectively, in $^{60}$Ni and $^{62}$Ni, as indicated by the position of the T=1 2+ ground state 2s1p shell.

In this work, we address the challenge of variance introduced during MLLT evaluation for assessing proposed improvements over baseline systems. The high level of variance in MLLT scores can lead to misleading assessments of systems. We investigate MLLT's susceptibility to random fluctuations and develop the J-K fold cross-validation technique to mitigate its impact. Our approach involves retraining and testing on shuffled portions of the test set, allowing us to produce more reliable comparisons between systems by averaging MLLT evaluation scores. We demonstrate this method's consistency by applying it to examine recent studies and validate our in findings with experiments designed to mimic various conditions, as well as experiments evaluating proposed and common alternatives in the context of Neural Question Answering. The results highlight the importance of managing variance in variance-prone tasks like Neural Question Answering.

This paper examines instructorsc pupils knowledge acquisition framework in the context of three primary components: instructors, pupils, and the knowledge transfer process. A comprehensive analysis is performed by exploring existing scholarship across disciplines including psychology, mathematics education, and human knowledge management. The underlying rationale for examining this field is rooted by the underlying value of instructorsc pupils framework in the knowledge management field. A detailed overview of existing research is presented which demonstrates the framework's utility in categorizing knowledge acquisition knowledge. A discussion is presented on the framework's utility in knowledge transfer processes as well as potential applications in the emerging instructorc pupils framework. A detailed analysis is presented which provides a direction for potential future investigations.

The probability edge potential, first introduced by Findlay and Kivela in 2020, has been demonstrated to facilitate efficient exact calculation of maximum a posteriori estimates in Bayesian analysis and optimization within graphical models. Our framework expands the scope of probability edge potential applications and control methods, providing a more in-depth examination of exact MAE computation under undirected Markov random fields. Our research indicates that exact inference for such structures can be achieved through the probability edge potential framework without the need for additional computation, allowing for various forms of optimization, including finding the mode of the posterior distribution. We have developed and released an open-source implementation of the probability edge potential framework in the GraphInferencePython package. Our methods for directed acyclic graphs and undirected Markov random fields have been compared, demonstrating the framework's efficiency through seven real-world datasets. The results show that our approach can calculate exact maximum a posteriori estimates in undirected Ising models without the need for further optimization, while existing methods require optimization even in simplified cases.

We reviewed the limitations of single-beam absorption spectroscopy by reviewing the physics and developed models to incorporate its constraints, specifically the beam's finite width and its ability to induce transitions both directly and through photon recoil. We created an in-depth examination of photon recoil using an alkali-earth vapor and ab initio methods, resulting in a usable reference for such effects. To verify our models, we compared them to multiple datasets from various experiments using an ultracold Sr vapor and a high-intensity laser beam, observing the finite beam's impact on absorption features and their symmetry around resonance frequencies. Although photon recoil can distort features in high-density vapors, it also leads to unbalanced features at low densities, making it identifiable and measurable.

When a fluid experiences fluctuating shear forces, the points where the fluid begins to lose stability and the points where it fully transitions are noticeably different. So far, this observation has been limited mainly to simple linear scenarios. As the amplitude of the fluid's changes increases, so do the complexities of the scenarios. This study investigates the shear buoyancy transition in a fluid influenced by both shear and rotation forces, as well as in scenarios involving both shear and surface tension forces. We find that the scaling factors for these transitions, in both cases, fall within the range of 5 to 10, highlighting their similarities. We propose that this overlap supports the concept of universal behavior in these fluid dynamics scenarios.

This homomorphism's image set has been found to correspond precisely to the racah parameters, which constitute a collection of homogeneous elements of degree 3 within the algebra $Z_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. This research investigates the objectiveivity of Google+ personalization when
attempting to completely neutralize its personalization features. It involves
two objective tests: the first is based on the concept that web pages randomly
selected for a given query should be evenly distributed under neutral settings,
and the second is grounded in the principle that the demographic characteristics
of web pages should match those of the general population for both neutral and
non-neutral conditions. Despite using different account types and given various
options, Google+ personalization fails to achieve neutrality, as it cannot
fully disable its personalization features and continuously personalizes
content even with personal signals disabled. It is concluded that Google+
cannot be considered an instrument for creating unbiased web page recommendations
and that it always personalizes for the user's benefit rather than providing
objective, relevant information. It is suggested that further research be done
to quantify the amount of relevant information a user may miss due to Google+
personalization.

A new type of particle accelerator combining ions and muons could reveal deeper scientific insights by taking advantage of the massive energy transfer possible in these collisions. In this research project, utilizing the PEP-II 1.8 TeV-class e+e- collider as a blueprint for producing high-energy muon beams in both directions, we predict that a 300 us long beam of 109 anti-deuterons will generate over 10 pb of a specific reaction - producing a top quark, another top quark, and two high-energy photons. The discovery of this reaction would significantly exceed current limits set by hadron colliders like the LHC. Another exciting possibility is that the same detector used in this experiment might be able to produce images of rare interactions involving strange particles, specifically producing two strange quarks and two anti-strange quarks along with two high-energy photons - also in excess of 100 events per year. Given its high energy and sensitivity to heavy particles, this unique muon-ion collider would be capable of producing over 100 events per year for the reaction in question, allowing researchers to study these rare interactions in detail.

A novel approach to automate the configuration of 4D (three-dimensional MRI plus respiratory effects) T2-weighted turbo spin-echo sequences is presented, enabling accurate and efficient scans for a wide range of patients without requiring manual intervention from radiologists. By creating a radiographic standards 3D reference model, the sequence parameters are automatically calculated to minimize variations in total scan time depending on individual patient factors, such as body size and breathing patterns. In simulated environments and real-world trials, this method consistently produced consistent scan durations across different patients and breath patterns, reliably producing 4D MRI images in a consistent amount of time. The 4D MR images produced using this technique offer consistent quality and allow for precise lesion detection and measurement. Overall, this automated framework ensures consistent, reliable, and personalized 4D T2-w TSE scans for patients, eliminating the need for them to hold their breath during the procedure.

Automatic testing for software often employs test metrics to identify failures in programs that correctly solve specific test cases. Currently, standard metrics like code coverage and tokenization calculate how much of the underlying source code is executed. In these calculations, metrics like code coverage determine source lines or blocks of the program that have been run. These methods include invisible, non-executed code, such as comments and string literals, in their calculations, which can confuse developers and direct them to unrunnable parts of the code when defects are found. We propose an accurate paired-permutation examination approach to generate an accurate metric indicating which code is executed by solving test cases, then we compare this to existing methods like code coverage in two different frameworks. In our studies, we discovered that the current metrics incorrectly include code lines with text inputs and we provided an adjusted calculation, called executed text lines (ETL), that only counts lines where code is actually run, which can be up to 3 times more effective in detecting errors than traditional metrics like TTL. We also developed an open-source tool, Met, to implement the accurate paired-permutation examination approach and made the ETL metric available for use in the under-analyzed automatic testing community.

This research provides continuous data for the cargo shipping industry, specifically for large vessel transactions, spanning the past five decades. Spreadsheets covering freight costs, newly built ships, second-hand vessels and scrap values by waterway and ship type are available for download at no cost. Historically, cargo shipping was a highly visible and economically significant industry, driving major mergers among U.S. shipping lines in 1967, 1970, and 1997. The compiled dataset proves valuable for studies on the dynamics between wages and output prices, the impact of freight prices on global economic activity, and the forces behind shifts in capital demand across different sectors.

A new class of distance metrics, called diverging distances, is introduced in this study, which strictly extend the concept of F-metrics. These distances enable the creation of statistical distances that increase between comparable distributions and can be computed efficiently using the Koul triangulation technique at O(nlog n) complexity. In comparison, existing methods using majorization have limitations in comparison complexity or require excessive memory usage. The proposed diverging distances have numerous potential uses in various fields, including computing lower bounds on sample sizes for hypothesis testing, determining minimum sample sizes for achieving specific statistical accuracy, and detecting copy number variations in next-generation sequencing data.

Deep Generative Models have advanced significantly in recent times, particularly
with the introduction of Variational Approaches and Adversarial Techniques.
However, despite their success with continuous data types, their effectiveness
with discrete data sets remains questionable. This study explores the
combination of a BERT-based stock prediction model with a VAE-GAN framework,
resulting in more accurate predictions and corrections of initial forecasts.
Experiments also conducted using a VAE model alone offered comparative data.
Findings indicate that integrating Adversarial Techniques provides better
outcomes than utilizing a VAE model alone, although they require extensive
computational resources. Furthermore, the study discusses difficulties
encountered when applying these models to text data and presents potential
applications along with limitations of the proposed approach.

We analyzed four potential sources of Single Higgs background: radiative single Higgs, non-resonant single Higgs, and single Higgs associated with photon or Z boson radiation, considering both diagonal and off-diagonal cases for $t^+t^+$, $t^+t^-$, and $t^-t^- final states. We begin by examining the stress-energy tensor for a symmetric tensor field representing classical gravity, which serves as the gravitational field in various theories. Next, we derive the equations of motion for this field from corresponding Lagrangians. There are multiple equivalent forms of these Lagrangians, and although they produce identical stress-energy tensors and equations of motion, their quantum quantum field theories may yield distinct results. We explore several common gravity quantum field theories, including massless gravity, Yang-Mills-gravity, and Einstein's gravity, highlighting the different outcomes they produce.

This study investigates the drag experienced by a cylindrical solid as it moves through a granular bed filled with fluid, moving slowly and perpendicular to the cylinder's axis. The drag coefficient, defined as the resistance a cylinder encounters while moving, is calculated based on the diameter of the cylinder, the size of the cylinder compared to the bed, the thickness of the layer of grains, and a number that accounts for the friction between the grains. As the cylinder moves, the drag it experiences can front-to-back symmetry be broken, meaning it experiences different resistance depending on the direction it moves. This study finds that this asymmetry mainly happens when the cylinder's diameter is close to the bed's diameter and the friction between the grains is high. It also discovers that this asymmetry results in a net force that is directed towards the outside, can cause the cylinder to move in a curved path, or cause it to rotate around its axis. This study aims to better understand the forces that act on cylindrical solids in beds of grains and provides a new, more accurate way to measure drag in these conditions.

To investigate the suitability of linear $p_T$-dependent hydrodynamics for describing heavy ion collisions, we used a multiphase transport (v3.6) to analyze triangular flow ($v_3$) in Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions at various energies. Our results show that v3.6 accurately replicates observed values of $v_3$, whereas a conventional transport model (AMPT) underestimates $v_3$ significantly. We found that a quadratic relationship between $v_3$ and initial triangular eccentricity ($\epsilon_3$) incorrectly predicts $v_3$ in Cu+Cu collisions but a linear relationship works well for Au+Au collisions. Our research also revealed a crossover from dominant second-order flow to triangular flow as collisions become more central. Additionally, we analyzed the sensitivity of $v_3/\epsilon_3$ to initial state assumptions and final state hydrodynamic effects using a superposition model and a modified v3.6 with an incorporated equation of state. Our analysis highlights the intricate interplay between geometry, flow, and heavy ion collision dynamics.

The ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is well-suited for measuring decay rareness and searching for new physics beyond the Standard Model through processes like CP violation. Recent results achieved with ATLAS include determining the rare decay $B^0_s \to \mu^+ \mu^-$ rate, an upper limit on the rare decay $B^0 \pi^+ \pi^0$, and an limit on the rare decay $B^0_s \pi^+ \pi^0$, as well as constraints on the CP-violating phase in $B^0_s \to \pi^+ \pi^0$. These achievements demonstrate the capability of ATLAS to push the boundaries of precision in beauty meson physics. This review delves into the recent achievements in measuring rare beauty meson decays and CP violation in the $B^0_s \to \pi^+ \pi^0$ process, anticipating the precision attainable with increased data collected by ATLAS.

Recently, logarithmic-finite element methods have seen significant advancement, particularly with linear elements showing notable efficiency and accuracy. This study builds upon existing work by examining and enhancing the preconditioning strategies for the resulting nonlinear systems. We employ the Newton method to address nonlinearity and investigate two prominent solvers within the Krylov family - Preconditioned Restricted Additive Schwarz Method (PRASAM) and Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient (PCG). Through various scenarios and refined preconditioners, we observe substantial improvements in performance when using PCG over just an identity matrix for preconditioning. These findings are supported by comprehensive numerical experiments across diverse conditions.

Accurate and non-invasive alignment of medical images acquired at different times is essential for various clinical applications. While registering a pre-operative 3D volume to a post-operative 3D surface is a crucial task for several procedures, it's a particularly challenging instance of non-rigid volume-to-surface registration. During laparoscopic surgeries, instrument punctures and tissue shifts caused by instrument insertion can significantly distort organ structures, complicating registration. In this study, a novel approach for aligning stomach images is presented, incorporating a simple and efficient biomechanical model that reverses the effects of instrument puncture and port-site distension. This model utilizes a simulation of pocket inflation, based on an inverse finite element simulation with inflated boundary conditions around the puncture and port-site areas. Bounding conditions for this simulation are determined through an optimized method. In addition, a non-biomechanical optimization step is performed to increase the likelihood of the volume fitting the surface, while ensuring the stomach aligns with physically feasible deformation. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through high-accuracy results in experimental data sets, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods in multiple evaluation metrics.
